Raincloud Plot with Plotly

Source: R/plot_raincloud_ly.R
plot_raincloud_ly.Rd

Draws an interactive raincloud plot using plotly. With option to show or hide each of half-violin density plots, boxplots, and scatter plots of the raw values.

Usage

plot_raincloud_ly(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  colors = NULL,
  show_density = TRUE,
  show_scatter = TRUE,
  show_box = TRUE,
  show_buttons = TRUE,
  show_legend = FALSE,
  density_side = c("right", "left"),
  density_width = 0.38,
  density_opacity = 0.45,
  scatter_layout = c("jitter", "dots", "center"),
  scatter_side = c("auto", "left", "right", "center"),
  scatter_size = 6,
  scatter_opacity = 0.65,
  jitter_width = 0.2,
  dot_binwidth = NULL,
  dot_spacing = 0.035,
  box_width = 0.16,
  boxpoints = FALSE,
  boxmean = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

x, y

Single strings naming columns of `data`. One must be numeric and the other categorical.

colors

Optional character vector of colours. A named vector is matched to group names; an unnamed vector is assigned in group order. If `NULL`, colours come from [grDevices::hcl.colors()].

show_density, show_scatter, show_box

Logical; whether each element is initially visible.

show_buttons

Logical; add buttons that toggle each element.

show_legend

Logical; show one legend entry per group.

density_side

Side of the group position on which the half-violin is drawn: `"right"` or `"left"`. For horizontal plots these are the upper and lower sides.

density_width

Maximum width of the half-violin, in units of the distance between groups.

density_opacity

Fill opacity of the density, between 0 and 1.

scatter_layout

Point placement: `"jitter"` (random), `"dots"` (stacked within bins) or `"center"` (on the group position).

scatter_side

Side of the group position on which points are placed: `"auto"` (opposite to the density), `"left"`, `"right"` or `"center"`.

scatter_size

Marker size.

scatter_opacity

Marker opacity, between 0 and 1.

jitter_width

Maximum jitter when `scatter_layout = "jitter"`.

dot_binwidth

Bin width along the numeric axis when `scatter_layout = "dots"`. If `NULL`, one thirtieth of the data range.

dot_spacing

Spacing between stacked dots when `scatter_layout = "dots"`.

box_width

Width of the boxplot.

boxpoints

Passed to [plotly::add_boxplot()]; `FALSE`, `"outliers"` or `"suspectedoutliers"`.

boxmean

Passed to [plotly::add_boxplot()]; `TRUE`, `FALSE` or `"sd"`.

...

Additional arguments passed to [plotly::plot_ly()].

Value

A plotly object.

Details

Exactly one of `x` or `y` must be numeric and the other categorical: * categorical `x` and numeric `y` give a vertical plot; * numeric `x` and categorical `y` give a horizontal plot.

Rows with missing values in either column are dropped. Group order follows the factor levels (unused levels are dropped), otherwise the order of first appearance. Each group uses one colour across all three elements.

With `scatter_layout = "dots"`, values are binned along the numeric axis and stacked along the categorical axis, which approximates stacked-dot displays without overlapping points. With `"jitter"` the positions are random, so use [set.seed()] for reproducible plots.

Elements switched off with `show_density`, `show_scatter` or `show_box` are still added to the plot, but start hidden, so that the buttons can reveal them.

Examples

set.seed(1)
plot_raincloud_ly(iris,
                  x = "Species",
                  y = "Sepal.Length",
                  scatter_layout = "jitter",
                  show_buttons = FALSE)



plot_raincloud_ly(iris,
                  x = "Sepal.Length",
                  y = "Species",
                  colors = c("#11A7F2", "#E00087", "#00bdaa"),
                  scatter_layout = "dots",
                  show_box = FALSE,
                  show_legend = TRUE) |>
  plotly::layout(yaxis = list(showticklabels = FALSE),
                 legend = list(x = 1, y = -0.2, xanchor = "right",
                               orientation = "h"))
